guard: the operator-global seed store announces what it WRITES and what it REMOVES, names the exact path, and stays silent when it copies nothing
why: FIVE MUTATIONS. Four break a guard; one models a failure that no single edit to the product can
produce. The distinction is stated because a reader who assumes all five are the same kind will
over-read the third.
M1 deletes the write announce, restoring exactly the defect #593 reports: the machine-wide payload
write happens and nothing in the output names a path outside the current directory.
M2 announces the destination as the STORE ROOT rather than the payload directory. The generic cell
still passes, because the root is a substring of nothing it needs; the exact-destination cell is the
one that reddens. That is the point of having both: a line that says 'something under here' is not
the disclosure the issue asks for.
M3 moves the announce onto the stager's IDEMPOTENT EARLY RETURN, so a re-seed that copies nothing
announces anyway. It reddens the reuse-path cell in the same-generation built-in add block. THIS
MUTATION IS REACHABLE AND THE FIXTURE PREVIOUSLY CLAIMED IT WAS NOT: an earlier version of this
file asserted that no command the suite drives reaches that early return. That was FALSE, and a
review lens demonstrated it live: the same-generation block strips a built-in from the manifest,
from disk and from both authority records while leaving its payload in the store, so the re-seed
calls the stager with an intact payload and takes the early return. Nothing asserted that block's
stderr, so a misplaced announce there passed green. The cell was added for that reason and this
mutation is what grades it.
M4 deletes the REMOVAL announce. The store's destructive step, dropping an unreferenced generation,
is a machine-wide delete performed by a command an operator ran for a local reason, and a silent
delete is worse than a silent write: the write at least leaves the thing it made.
M5 is the one that MODELS a failure rather than breaking a guard, and it is here because the
steady-state cell would otherwise be ungraded. That path is protected by two independent layers,
the reconcile returning NOOP without calling the stager and the stager's own early return, so no
single edit makes a steady-state boot copy bytes. M5 emits the line from the NOOP return itself,
which is precisely the failure the cell exists to catch.
ORDER, because the suite is fail-fast and a red on the wrong leg is not a kill of the assertion
named. Each mutation's expectRed is the FIRST assertion that mutation can reach: M1 and M2 reach
the first-boot cells, M5 reaches the second-boot cell in the same block, M3 reaches nothing until
the same-generation block, and M4 nothing until the GC block.
WHAT THIS STILL DOES NOT PROVE. It grades the announces, not the isolation: nothing here shows that
XDG_CONFIG_HOME actually relocates the store, which is existing behaviour this change documents
rather than adds. It also does not grade the extensions-prefix install on the reconcile path, which
is announced only inside the `ext add` child whose stderr the parent drops on success; that is
pre-existing and named in the PR body rather than fixed here.
